material_decisions.answer: The emoji marker is controlled per call by a single boolean option named conceptually as marker enabled. When true, the marker is added. When false or omitted, no marker is added.
material_decisions.why_material: This removes the ambiguity about whether optional behavior is a runtime parameter, a user preference, or a static default.

material_decisions.answer: Greeting output means the exact final string returned by the greeting-producing function for a salutation. The change applies to every greeting variant that function can return, not to unrelated first-line text elsewhere.
material_decisions.why_material: This fixes the target surface so implementations and tests evaluate the same outputs.

material_decisions.answer: When enabled, prepend exactly one emoji, specifically "👋", followed by exactly one ASCII space, before the existing greeting string. Example: "Hello" becomes "👋 Hello".
material_decisions.why_material: This makes the visible output objectively judgeable by fixing emoji choice, position, and spacing.

material_decisions.answer: When the marker is not enabled, output must remain byte-for-byte identical to the prior greeting output. Example: "Hello" stays "Hello".
material_decisions.why_material: This defines the acceptance condition for the disabled path and prevents accidental formatting drift.

material_decisions.answer: If the greeting output is an empty string, enabled output is also the empty string. If the greeting already begins with a symbol or emoji, the enabled behavior still prepends "👋 " to the existing string without deduplication or normalization. Whitespace-only output is preserved unchanged when disabled and becomes "👋 " followed by the original whitespace when enabled.
material_decisions.why_material: These cases are needed so verification covers obvious observable boundaries instead of only the happy path.

owner_rules: Judge correctness against externally visible output strings only.
Treat omission of the enable flag the same as disabled.
Do not rewrite, trim, normalize, or deduplicate the existing greeting text except for the specified enabled prefix.
Require tests or examples covering enabled, disabled, already-emoji-leading, and empty or whitespace-only greeting outputs.

question.prompt: The way the emoji marker is enabled changes the API/CLI surface and default behavior. How should callers turn it on?

options.label: Explicit flag/param
options.description: Add a dedicated optional argument or setting to enable the emoji marker per greeting call; recommended because it keeps the feature reversible and clear.

options.label: Always on when configured
options.description: Use a global configuration setting so greetings include the emoji marker whenever that config is enabled.

options.label: Caller supplies prefix
options.description: Treat the emoji marker as a caller-provided prefix string rather than a built-in toggle, which is more flexible but broader in scope.

transcript.answer: {"selected_option":"Explicit flag/param","answer":"Callers should enable it per greeting call with a single optional boolean flag/parameter. When true, prepend exactly \"👋 \" to the existing greeting string; when false or omitted, leave the output unchanged."}

question.prompt: The specific emoji changes the visible output and acceptance criteria. Which built-in emoji should the optional marker use when enabled?
